questions.question: Which of the following describes the three main subatomic particles that make up an atom?
questions.explanation: The three main particles are protons, neutrons, and electrons.

questions.question: Which part of an atom contains protons and neutrons?
questions.explanation: The nucleus contains protons and neutrons.

questions.question: Where can negatively charged electrons be found in an atom?

options.label: B
options.text: Outside the nucleus, in the electron cloud

options.label: C
options.text: Together with neutrons inside the nucleus

options.label: D
options.text: Only at the center of the atom

questions.explanation: Electrons are found outside the nucleus.

questions.question: What is the electrical charge of a proton?
questions.explanation: A proton has a positive charge.

questions.question: Which subatomic particle has no electrical charge?
questions.explanation: A neutron has no electrical charge.

questions.question: Which statement correctly compares the charges of protons and electrons?

options.label: C
options.text: Protons are positive while electrons are negative.

options.label: D
options.text: Protons are neutral while electrons are positive.

questions.explanation: Protons are positive; electrons are negative.

questions.question: An atom has 12 protons. What is its atomic number?
questions.explanation: Atomic number equals the number of protons.

questions.question: An atom contains 8 protons and 8 neutrons. What is its mass number?
An atom contains equal numbers of protons and electrons. What can be concluded about its overall electrical charge?
questions.explanation: Equal numbers of protons and electrons produce a neutral atom.

questions.question: An atom has 3 protons and 2 electrons. What is its overall electrical charge?
questions.explanation: 3 positive charges and 2 negative charges give a net charge of +1.

questions.question: This positively charged subatomic particle is found inside the nucleus of an atom.
This neutral subatomic particle is also found inside the nucleus.
This is the region of an atom where negatively charged electrons can be found.
An atom contains 15 protons. What is its atomic number?
An atom contains 10 protons and 12 neutrons. What is its mass number?
Enumerate the three main subatomic particles that form an atom.
Give the two relationships used to determine the atomic number and mass number of an atom.
questions.answer:
Atomic number = number of protons (equal to the number of electrons in a neutral atom).
Mass number = number of protons + number of neutrons.

questions.question: Enumerate the three subatomic particles and indicate the electrical charge of each.
questions.answer:
Proton – Positive (+1)
Neutron – Neutral (0)
Electron – Negative (−1)

questions.question: An atom contains protons, which are positively charged, and electrons, which are negatively charged. Explain how an atom can remain electrically neutral despite containing charged particles. Include the relationship between the numbers of protons and electrons in your explanation.
questions.answer: An atom can remain electrically neutral when the number of positively charged protons is equal to the number of negatively charged electrons. Their opposite electrical charges balance each other, resulting in an overall charge of zero.

questions.question: Why is it important to understand the structure of an atom even though atoms cannot be seen with our naked eyes? Explain your answer and describe how an atomic model can help represent the arrangement and location of subatomic particles.
questions.answer: Understanding atomic structure helps learners understand what matter is made of and how its smallest components are organized. Although atoms cannot be seen with our naked eyes, atomic models help represent their structure by showing the nucleus, protons, neutrons, and electrons in the electron cloud.
